messages:
maria: heads-up — we're getting a flood of dropped connections in the eastus4 GPU pool since the autoscaler burst at 09:12. Apps report RPC errors and reconnect storms.

ajay: saw it too, lots of east-west between model-serving pods when new replicas warmed. packet loss + high latency reported by perf trace.

kenji: quick check — `sudo cat /proc/sys/net/netfilter/nf_conntrack_count` => ~65534, `nf_conntrack_max` at 65536. conntrack is pegged.

laura: ouch. looks like SNAT/conntrack exhaustion from ephemeral port fan-out during cold starts (clients -> many new pods). any idea why traffic isn't staying local?

ajay: kube-proxy in iptables mode fell back to userspace on some nodes after OOM of kube-proxy pod, looks like hairpin + cross-node routing triggered. that's why east-west is going through SNAT.

maria: logs show kube-proxy restarts ~09:11 on three nodes in the GPU pool. deploy-bot also did a config update 09:10 (no rollout intended for that pool).

kenji: short-term mitigation: increase `net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max` and reduce `nf_conntrack_tcp_timeout_established` for these nodes. running these now via ad-hoc ssh: `sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=262144` and `sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_tcp_timeout_established=600`

laura: can also `kubectl -n kube-system rollout restart daemonset/kube-proxy` on the affected nodes once conntrack headroom exists — switch back to ipvs if possible to reduce conntrack churn.

maria: doing the restart in canary first. I'll also cordon one node and repro to confirm local routing.

kenji: long-term: consider Cilium/eBPF to avoid SNAT for intra-cluster pod-to-pod, or enable `externalTrafficPolicy=Local` patterns for service types we can control. Also look at autoscaler smoothing to avoid huge simultaneous cold-starts.

ajay: costing note — this pattern massively increases egress SNAT and adds NAT SNAT concurrency. If we hit this regularly, we should invest in an SNAT gateway (dedicated NAT instances) or add more host ports / hostNetwork for the hottest models.

maria: agreed. I'll open a short ops doc with proposed mitigations + perf numbers. For now the sysctl bumps + kube-proxy restart dropped conntrack by 70% and errors have subsided.

sre-bot: incident-create: eastus4-snat-throttle-1951234567 — severity: P2, owner: maria, runbook: /ops/runbooks/snat-overflow.md

laura: leaving notes — followups: autoscaler policy, kube-proxy mode audit across GPU pool, baseline conntrack headroom telemetry, and evaluate eBPF/Calico CNI tradeoffs.

maria: thanks all, monitoring for 30m then we'll uncordon and re-evaluate. :thumbsup:
